status_assessment.basis: The architectural firm that renovated the site states that the church and hall were deconsecrated in 2011 and that the current owners bought the site in 2019. It says the hall has been converted to a residence and the church is to become a three-bedroom family home. No source I opened shows worship after 2011. This rests on one secondary source (the architect's project pages), which is internally consistent. Diocesan or newspaper confirmation of the deconsecration is still needed.
status_assessment.osm_stale_basis: The current OSM version (v2, 2024-12-07) still tags the way amenity=place_of_worship with religion and denomination, a contact phone number and a church name. The 2024 edit changed only the phone format. By the architect's account the site was deconsecrated in 2011 and has been in private residential ownership since 2019. The OSM record therefore no longer describes the site as the sources do; a disused or former-church tagging would fit better.

run_manifest.notes: claude session 1392358a-2ff4-4e95-be56-c6dd56d3cd2f; num_turns 25; permission_denials 0 | The evidence for closure is the architect's own account of the renovation, not an institutional record. The firm is a private architectural practice (barryconnordesign.co.nz), outside the allowlist, and I weighted it as secondary. The next step is to confirm the 2011 deconsecration and the sale through the Anglican Diocese of Christchurch or Anglican Life, or a Press or Stuff report. The two Barry Connor pages are undated, and the church conversion is described as 'upcoming', so its present state is unknown. Several fetch-tool outputs of the hall page came back paraphrased rather than verbatim. I quoted only short fragments that the tool marked as direct quotations, and these should be checked against the live page. Heritage NZ list entry 2644, returned by search, is St Columba in Grey Lynn, Auckland, and is unrelated. The OSM start_date=1905 is uncorroborated; Papers Past search pages returned no readable content through the fetch tool, so it could not be checked there. The parish is probably the Anglican Parish of Hurunui (Diocese of Christchurch), but no opened source confirms this, so I have made no organisation_link claim. OSM editor usernames and the phone number are omitted under the privacy and institutional-contact rules.
